slides.fact: _There's no cow on the ice_: the Swedish way to say there's no rush.

slides.title: Where the cow comes from
slides.body:
The full saying is *ingen ko på isen så länge rumpan är i land*: no cow on the ice as long as its rear end is on land.

A cow out on thin ice is a real problem. A cow with its back half still on shore can easily back off. So relax, nothing is wrong yet.

slides.sv: Vi har gott om tid, det är *ingen ko på isen*.
slides.en: We have plenty of time, there's no rush.

caption:
Det är ingen ko på isen: literally "there's no cow on the ice". It means there's no need to worry or hurry.

The longer version adds "så länge rumpan är i land": as long as its rear end is still on land.

What's the strangest idiom in your language?
